routes.name: Silk Road to the Americas
routes.summary: A counterfactual maritime extension of the Silk Road across the Pacific, linking Tang/Song China directly to Mesoamerica centuries before Columbus.
routes.premise: What if trans-Pacific navigation had matured a millennium early, carrying silk and porcelain to the Maya and Mexica in exchange for cacao, maize and turquoise?
sources: Speculative educational overlay — not a historical trade route.
Menzies, G. (2002). 1421: The Year China Discovered the World (a contested popular hypothesis).

routes.name: Trans-Atlantic Gold Route
routes.summary: A counterfactual continuation of the Trans-Saharan gold trade across the Atlantic from the Mali Empire to the South American coast.
routes.premise: What if Mansa Musa's rumoured Atlantic fleets had reached Brazil, extending the West African gold-and-salt economy into the New World?
sources: Speculative educational overlay — not a historical trade route.
Based on the disputed traditions of Abu Bakr II's Atlantic expeditions.

routes.name: Polar Amber Road
routes.summary: A counterfactual Arctic trade corridor linking Baltic amber producers to Siberian and North Pacific networks over an ice-free polar route.
routes.premise: What if a warmer early-medieval Arctic had opened a navigable polar road, tying Norse, Finno-Ugric and Siberian traders into one amber-and-fur network?
sources: Speculative educational overlay — not a historical trade route.
